title: Is Duolingo Good for Spanish? What Learners Should Know

body_text: Duolingo is one of the most downloaded language apps in the world, and for many people, it's the first stop on the road to Spanish fluency. Short lessons, gamified streaks, and a low barrier to entry make it easy to start. But ease of use and actual progress are not always the same thing, and anyone serious about finding the best way to learn conversational Spanish will want to know what Duolingo genuinely delivers versus where it falls short. The app builds familiarity with vocabulary and basic grammar, but it rarely pushes learners to produce spoken Spanish with confidence. Real conversational ability comes from practicing the way people actually speak, not just tapping the right answer on a screen. For learners who want to close that gap, learn Spanish with Parrot , a program built around the kind of listening and speaking practice that turns passive recognition into real fluency. Table of Contents Why So Many Learners Ask Whether Duolingo Is Good for Spanish Where Duolingo Excels and Where It Falls Short Why Some Learners Plateau With Duolingo What Actually Helps Learners Become Conversational Is Duolingo the Right Tool for Your Learning Goals? How Parrot Helps You Move Beyond Language Exercises Start Learning Spanish Today Summary Duolingo's scale reflects genuine demand for accessible language learning, with over 500 million registered users worldwide and Spanish consistently ranking as the most-studied language in the United States. But completion rates tell a different story. Less than 0.1% of users actually finish their courses, meaning the vast majority stop somewhere between motivated beginner and conversational speaker. The research on conversational turns points to something most learners overlook. Children who experienced more back-and-forth conversational exchange showed a 14% to 29% increase in brain activity in Broca's area, the region directly tied to language processing. That finding suggests active speaking practice physically reshapes how the brain handles language in ways that passive study cannot replicate. Reaching conversational proficiency in Spanish, a Category I language, requires roughly 600 to 750 hours of study according to Scott H. Young's analysis of language acquisition research. The quality of those hours matters as much as the volume. Hours spent in controlled, scaffolded environments build familiarity with exercises, not the mental flexibility that authentic Spanish demands. Even Duolingo's most advanced Spanish courses cap out at around B2 proficiency on the language-learning scale, short of C2 fluency. B2 covers structured conversations on familiar topics. C2 means following fast-moving native speech, catching humor, and responding without searching for words. That structural ceiling matters for anyone whose goal sits at genuine conversational ability. Learners who plateau with app-based study tend to stall in the A2 to B1 range, the beginner-to-intermediate band, which is precisely where the jump to authentic comprehension becomes necessary. At that level, the controlled environment of structured lessons has been buffering learners from fast speech, regional accents, and dropped words. Stepping outside that buffer makes the gap visible quickly. Parrot's Learn Spanish program addresses this gap by using short-form video immersion grounded in comprehensible input research, giving learners repeated exposure to authentic, natural speech within the same 10 to 15 minutes of daily practice that most structured apps already occupy. Why So Many Learners Ask Whether Duolingo Is Good for Spanish Duolingo's popularity is hard to ignore . According to the Duolingo Blog , the platform has over 500 million learners worldwide, with Spanish consistently ranking as one of its most studied languages . This scale raises the question: does it work? The answer is more complicated than the download numbers suggest. "The platform has over 500 million learners worldwide, with Spanish consistently ranking as one of its most studied languages." — Duolingo Blog 🔑 Takeaway: 500 million users is a staggering number, but popularity and effectiveness are not the same thing. The real question is whether those learners are achieving meaningful fluency in Spanish . 💡 Key Insight: When an app reaches 500 million downloads , it's essential to separate marketing success from learning outcomes : the two can tell different stories. Why do streaks and XP points fall short of real conversation? The gap lies between what an app measures and what a learner needs. Duolingo tracks streaks, XP points, and lesson completions—metrics that feel rewarding but don't guarantee real-world ability. A learner who finishes every Spanish unit can still freeze when a native speaker responds quickly, uses regional expressions, or runs sentences together without pausing. Completing exercises differs from processing real speech in real time. Most learners sense this gap without naming it. They practice daily, earn streaks, and still feel stuck when Spanish appears outside the app. That frustration signals that the method behind practice matters more than consistency alone. The Duolingo Blog notes that 34 hours of Duolingo Spanish equals a full university semester, a genuine achievement. But a semester of university Spanish rarely makes people conversational either. Does studying Spanish as a subject build real fluency? The common approach treats language learning as a subject to study rather than a skill to develop. Learners read rules, translate sentences, and match words to pictures—building conscious knowledge about Spanish. Fluent speakers, however, don't consciously recall grammar rules mid-conversation. They've internalized language through repeated exposure to comprehensible input in real speech. Apps built around gamification rarely replicate that process. Parrot's Learn Spanish program addresses this directly using short-form video immersion grounded in Dr. Stephen Krashen's comprehensible input research, building subconscious fluency rather than surface-level recognition. The question "Is Duolingo good for Spanish?" persists because learners want to know whether their daily habit will enable actual conversations, not higher scores. The answer depends on what kind of Spanish ability they're trying to build. What surprises most people is not what Duolingo gets wrong, but how specific its strengths and limitations are. Where Duolingo Excels and Where It Falls Short Duolingo is great at building vocabulary and reinforcing grammar patterns through smart habit design . However, it has real limits when you need to understand native speakers at full speed or discuss real-world topics . "Duolingo excels at vocabulary building and habit formation — but falls short when learners face the demands of full-speed native conversation and real-world fluency ." — Key Insight Duolingo performs well in foundational language skills but has limitations in real-world communication: Vocabulary building – Strong performance through repeated exposure and practice. Grammar pattern reinforcement – Strong support for developing basic language structures. Habit and consistency design – Excellent at encouraging daily practice through engagement features. Understanding native speakers at full speed – Weaker performance due to limited exposure to natural, fast-paced conversations. Real-world topic discussion – Limited ability to prepare learners for open-ended conversations and practical discussions. 🎯 Key Point: Duolingo is one of the best tools for building a vocabulary foundation and staying consistent — but it is not a complete path to conversational fluency . 💡 Tip: Use Duolingo for daily habit reinforcement and vocabulary , but supplement it with native listening practice and real conversation to close the fluency gap . What Duolingo actually does well According to the 2025 Duolingo Language Report , Spanish is the most studied language on Duolingo in the United States, with millions of learners. The app addresses a genuine problem: most people abandon language learning within weeks because the habit fails to take root. Duolingo's streak system, bite-sized lessons, and progress indicators are designed to solve this—and they do. Since consistency is essential for language skill development, Duolingo delivers it more effectively than most alternatives. The spaced repetition system underlying those lessons deserves credit. It spaces vocabulary review across time intervals that match how human memory consolidates information, so words learned in week one are more likely to stay with you in month three. That is learning science, not gamification dressed up as education. Where the method starts to break down The failure point is specific: Duolingo teaches you to recognize Spanish under controlled conditions, not to process it in the wild. A lesson presents one sentence at a time, at a readable pace, with clear visual context. A conversation with a native speaker in Mexico City provides none of those supports. Most learners handle this by practicing more in the app, hoping that more practice will translate into fluency. Instead, they become proficient at Duolingo, a different skill than speaking Spanish. Apps like Parrot use short-form video immersion to expose learners to authentic, natural speech within the same 10 to 15 minutes of daily practice, connecting the habit loop Duolingo builds to the comprehensible input that produces conversational ability. Does completing the full Spanish course lead to fluency? The 2025 Duolingo Language Report notes that Duolingo offers over 100 languages across more than 40 languages of instruction. Offering many languages differs from helping learners achieve proficiency. A learner who completes the entire Spanish course will have learned thousands of words and hundreds of grammar patterns, yet will likely struggle to understand a fast conversation between two friends. This skill requires exposure to real, unscripted speech. What happens when learners clear the barrier and still feel stuck? This is not a flaw in Duolingo's execution but a limit of its design philosophy. The app was built to lower the barrier to starting, and it succeeds. The question worth considering is what happens to learners once they clear that barrier and still feel stuck. But what happens inside the brain when a learner pushes past that stuck feeling is more surprising than most people expect. Most learners who get stuck with Duolingo aren't lacking discipline or aptitude : they're hitting the natural ceiling of a method designed to start the journey , not complete it. According to Ankur Garg on LinkedIn , citing Duolingo's own data , less than 0.1% of users actually complete their courses, meaning the vast majority stop somewhere between motivated beginner and conversational speaker . The platform is built for habit formation , not language mastery . ⚠️ Warning: If you're relying on Duolingo streaks to reach conversational ability, you're approaching the ceiling of what the method can deliver , regardless of consistency. Where the progress stalls The failure point is almost always the same: learners confuse recognizing Spanish with producing it. Matching words to pictures feels like progress, but recognition and recall are different thinking skills. Recognizing "quiero" in a multiple-choice prompt is far easier than retrieving it from memory mid-conversation while tracking what someone just said. The gap between those two things is where most learners get stuck. Why do streaks stop pushing you forward? Streaks make this worse. When keeping a streak becomes the daily goal, learners gravitate toward shorter lessons and familiar exercises—minimal friction. This preserves the streak count but prevents the brain from entering the discomfort where real learning happens. Consistency with the wrong approach builds bad habits faster. Ankur Garg's analysis notes that engaged learners plateau in the A2-B1 range, where the jump to real comprehension becomes necessary and structured app exercises are no longer sufficient. At A2, you have enough vocabulary to feel competent within the app's controlled environment. But that environment has shielded you from the messy, fast, accent-varied reality of actual Spanish. Step outside it, and the gap becomes visible immediately. What happens when learners double down on the wrong approach? Most learners respond by doing more: more lessons, longer sessions, harder difficulty settings. The same brain pathways get strengthened while the pathways needed for real-time listening and speaking remain underdeveloped. Apps like Parrot address this gap by using short-form video immersion grounded in comprehensible input research, so learners encounter Spanish through meaningful, contextual exposure rather than isolated drills. Why is waiting until you feel ready the wrong strategy? Speaking practice is what most learners delay too long. The reasoning sounds logical: improve first, then speak. But speaking is not the reward at the end of language learning—it is the training ground. Waiting until you feel ready is like waiting to feel comfortable before learning to swim. The discomfort is not a sign you are unprepared. It is the work itself. What happens inside the brain when learners commit to discomfort is more surprising than most people expect. What Actually Helps Learners Become Conversational Being able to speak Spanish naturally requires three things: comprehensible input, real conversation, and repeated practice until your brain stops translating and thinks in Spanish . No single app can do all three. Successful learners combine structured tools with real-world exposure and regular speaking practice. Why does real conversation reshape the brain differently than passive study? According to the Expressable Learning Center , children who engaged in back-and-forth conversations showed a 14% to 29% increase in brain activity in Broca's area, the region directly connected to language processing. Conversation physically changes how the brain handles language in ways that listening alone cannot. Listening to Spanish is helpful; responding in Spanish creates real change. Why does producing language matter more than consuming it? Most learners focus on comfort: consuming content, completing exercises, reviewing vocabulary . These feel productive, but production—generating language under real-time pressure—forces the brain to retrieve and automate what it has absorbed. Comprehension and production are related but distinct skills, and treating one as a substitute for the other is where most learners get stuck. Why does the quality of your Spanish input matter as much as the volume? The familiar approach to building Spanish—logging study time, finishing lessons, tracking streaks—has a limit. The gap appears when learners realize that completing exercises does not prepare them for real conversation, where speakers talk fast, skip words, use slang, and do not wait for you to catch up. According to Scott H. Young , reaching conversational proficiency in a Category I language like Spanish requires 600 to 750 hours of study, and the quality of those hours determines whether that time builds real fluency or surface familiarity. Apps that drip-feed controlled sentences in controlled environments fill hours without building the mental flexibility that authentic Spanish demands. What actually breaks through the ceiling when more lessons don't? Most learners respond by adding more structured lessons, assuming volume will break through the ceiling. What works is shifting input toward authentic, unscaffolded Spanish: real conversations, native-speed video, podcasts without transcripts. That shift is uncomfortable at first, which is why it works. Apps like Parrot use short-form video immersion to deliver comprehensible input the way the brain acquires language: in context, at natural pace, in the 10 to 15 minutes most learners already have in their day. Speaking practice is not a reward for being ready Learners typically treat speaking as the finish line rather than the training ground, waiting until grammar feels solid , vocabulary feels wide enough, or fear feels manageable. None of those conditions arrive on schedule. Conversational turns create language skill, not the other way around. Research directly reinforces this: language development depends not on the volume absorbed but on active exchange. Start speaking before you feel ready, because readiness builds through doing, not before it. The question is whether the tools you are using align with this science. title: The Muslims Still Standing: Every Muslim Player Left at This World Cup
summary: Morocco may be out, but Muslims are still shaping the World Cup. Meet every Muslim player left in the tournament & why they're worth cheering for.
body_text: The Atlas Lions are home, the group chat has moved through all five stages of grief, and four teams remain: France, Spain, England, and Argentina. Not exactly the ummah’s dream bracket. But look closer at these squads and you’ll find something worth watching for — because scattered across the biggest stage in sport, our people are still standing. Some of them are the biggest stars in the world. One of them just made history. And one of them turns 19 today. Lamine Yamal — Spain 🇪🇸 Looking for your soulmate? You won’t find your soulmate on this blog post but you might find them on Muzz - the world’s biggest Muslim dating and marriage app. Sign Up muzz Start with the birthday boy. Yamal was born on July 13, 2007 — yes, today — to a Moroccan father from Larache and an Equatorial Guinean mother, raised in part by the Moroccan grandmother who nurtured his faith. He became the first player in Spain’s history to fast Ramadan while on international duty, with his own coach confirming it on the record. When he scored his first World Cup goal, he went straight into sujood in front of a packed stadium. When crowds targeted him with discriminatory chants earlier this year, his answer was simple: “I am Muslim, alhamdulillah.” And in May, he stood on top of Barcelona’s title parade bus waving a Palestinian flag while politicians fumed. Eighteen years old when he did all of it. Our Moroccan king, and he knows it. Ousmane Dembélé — France 🇫🇷 The reigning Ballon d’Or winner is a practising Muslim, born in Normandy to a Malian father and a Senegalese-Mauritanian mother. The stat sheet speaks for itself — but the detail that tells you who he is came back in 2018, when it was widely reported that he put his World Cup earnings toward building a mosque in his mother’s hometown in Mauritania. Most players buy a car. Dembélé built a house of Allah. France the state makes life hard for its Muslims; France the team doesn’t exist without them. Djed Spence — England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 History, quietly made: the Tottenham fullback is the first Muslim to ever play for England’s senior men’s team — in over 150 years of English international football. He’s said he hopes young Muslims see him and realize they can make it too. Every barrier broken makes the next kid’s path easier. When England line up on Wednesday, that’s what’s on the pitch. William Saliba, Ibrahima Konaté & Rayan Cherki — France 🇫🇷 Saliba is the quiet one. He fasts during Ramadan even on matchdays, once delayed an interview until after his Jummah prayers, and performed Umrah — all without ever making a speech about it. Some dawah is done entirely in actions. Konaté anchors the defense beside him, and Cherki, the Algerian-heritage playmaker, supplies the flair. Together with Dembélé, they’re the Muslim core of a squad from a country that keeps passing laws against its own Muslim citizens. Their players are French when they win and “foreign” when they lose. Watch them win anyway. The fixtures, then Tuesday brings France vs Spain — Muslims on both sides of the ball, so the deen advances no matter what (root for the birthday boy anyway). Wednesday it’s England vs Argentina — Spence carrying it alone against a squad offering us nothing. You know what to do. The part that actually matters There’s a reason these stories land so hard right now. Across Europe, being visibly Muslim gets legislated, debated, and chanted at. And then a teenager scores at a World Cup and puts his forehead on the grass in front of a billion people. Saliba delays interviews for Jummah and lets that speak. Spence walks through a door that was closed for a century and a half. None of them asked to be symbols. All of them are proof. So make dua for the boys carrying it this week. Make dua for Palestine, always. And while your hands are raised — add a quick “… and ya Allah, my naseeb too .” Might as well ask for it all. 🤲 Somewhere out there, your person is also planning their semifinal watch schedule. Imagine syncing calendars for the final. Start with Muzz — where the Ummah finds love.

title: Giving Back to Chicago’s Youth: Ginny Kowalczyk and The Night Ministry
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_text: Ginny Kowalczyk, Manager, Market Data Services, was first introduced to The Night Ministry in 2016 through a Securities Traders Association of Chicago (STAC) board member. They had been volunteering at The Night Ministry and told Ginny about the value and impact of the organization on the local community. She learned that The Night Ministry provides healthcare, meaningful connection and housing support to individuals facing homelessness and poverty in the community and was inspired to begin volunteering. Over the years Ginny became more involved with The Crib, a branch of The Night Ministry that specializes in providing a safe overnight shelter for young adults ages 18 to 24 who are typically a part of the LGBTQ+ community. Ginny supports The Crib through breakfast and dinner meal donations. She usually volunteers on the weekends and will cook or pick up breakfast and dinner to bring and serve to the residents. “Seeing a smile on their faces for a warm meal reinforces my commitment to The Night Ministry,” she says. “I’m glad I can help improve the lives of the youth in Chicago who don’t have a home to go to or a meal to eat.” After seeing the impact of her volunteer efforts with The Crib, Ginny hopes to volunteer with other branches of The Night Ministry that support homeless mothers and young children to continue giving back to her community. “I really value the hands-on nature of The Night Ministry and the way they provide resources to help people transition to stable housing,” she says. “I’m excited to find additional ways to stay involved and make an impact.” Ginny received Cboe’s 2025 Outstanding Community Service Award in recognition of her continued volunteer efforts. As part of the award, Cboe will donate $5,000 to The Crib a branch of The Night Ministry to support essential needs for residents including bedding, clothing items and basic necessities for daily living. There are numerous ways to get involved with The Night Ministry, learn more today.

HOUSTON and LONDON, July 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Baker Hughes Company (Nasdaq: BKR) ("Baker Hughes" or the "Company") announced results today for the second quarter of 2026. "Baker Hughes delivered another strong quarter, reflecting the breadth of our portfolio and continued momentum across data center, gas infrastructure, and upstream markets. Disciplined execution and our ability to effectively navigate ongoing Middle East challenges contributed to Adjusted EBITDA exceeding the high end of our guidance range. Looking ahead, favorable underlying fundamentals support our confidence in achieving the midpoint of our full-year guidance as we continue to manage through the Middle East uncertainty." "IET delivered another exceptional quarter of orders, with record bookings doubling year-over-year to $7.1 billion and backlog increasing 19% to a new all-time high. The strength was driven by robust demand across Power Systems and LNG, with particularly strong momentum in power generation. Given broadening customer demand, a growing pipeline across industrial and energy infrastructure markets, and our decision to further expand capacity, we are raising our full-year IET order guidance and increasing our Horizon 2(1) IET orders outlook to more than $45 billion." "OFSE delivered an impressive quarter, with EBITDA exceeding the high end of our guidance range despite a complex operating environment. Increased activity and higher product shipments late in the quarter in the Middle East, along with solid performance in North America land and Latin America, drove the upside and demonstrated the resilience and durability of our portfolio despite higher inflationary costs." "Our second-quarter performance further reinforces confidence in Baker Hughes’ strategic direction. Energy security and rising power demand are driving investment across both energy and industrial value chains, and our expanding portfolio is increasingly aligned with the most attractive growth opportunities across our core end markets." "The successful closing of the Chart acquisition marks a major milestone in our evolution as a leading industrialized energy solutions company. Chart enhances our capabilities in thermal management, air and gas handling, compression and lifecycle services, while expanding our reach across attractive core and adjacent markets. The addition of Chart further advances our portfolio, broadens our growth opportunities, and enhances our ability to create long-term value for customers and shareholders. Quarter Highlights Executing our portfolio management strategy Announced the sale of Waygate Technologies to Hexagon, in an all-cash transaction for approximately $1.45 billion, before customary closing adjustments. In July, completed the previously announced purchase of Chart Industries, Inc. (NYSE: GTLS) in an all-cash transaction. The acquisition enhances Baker Hughes' portfolio with highly complementary technologies and expands exposure to attractive industrial and energy markets, while increasing the Company's installed base and recurring aftermarket opportunities. Key awards and technology achievements Leveraging enterprise-wide capabilities Advanced large-scale geothermal development in North America through a commercial agreement with Mantle Reach Power, a dedicated geothermal development company backed by EnCap Energy Transition Fund III. With the goal to install up to 500 megawatts of power in the next five years, the Company will act as an integrated subsurface solution provider, and Mantle Reach Power will lead project development, ownership and financing. Industrial & Energy Technology Industrial & Energy Technology (“IET”) secured important awards and agreements across diverse end markets and capabilities. Received a major Venture Global award to provide six liquefied natural gas (LNG) blocks, for a total of 12 liquefaction modules. Each block is based on two single mixed-refrigerant (SMR) liquefaction modules and related compression trains featuring Baker Hughes' advanced centrifugal compressor technology, as well as cold boxes, air coolers and integrated control systems, building on the successful track record of delivering critical energy infrastructure in Louisiana. Secured substantial awards from Cheniere and Bechtel that highlight Baker Hughes’ full-lifecycle LNG capabilities, including liquefaction equipment for Sabine Pass Train 7, as well as a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit and fleet-wide gas turbine upgrades across the facility. The awards are expected to support approximately 6 MTPA of additional LNG production capacity. Strengthened its position in floating LNG through a significant award from Golar to supply four PGT25 gas turbine-driven refrigerant compressor trains for a 3.5 MTPA floating LNG facility, marking the fourth Golar vessel to utilize Baker Hughes' liquefaction solutions. Extended a significant, multi-year services agreement with Nigeria LNG to enhance the reliability and efficiency of the project's critical Train 7 turbomachinery equipment. Received a major award from Dynamis Power Solutions, including 76 NovaLT™16 gas turbines, for approximately 1.3 GW of capacity for its hypermobile power solutions for a wide range of data center and oil & gas applications in North America. Signed a multi-year strategic agreement with Kodiak Gas Services, including an initial major award supporting 1 GW of power generation capacity and a broader framework providing a pathway for up to 1.8 GW over time. The initial order leverages Baker Hughes' NovaLT™16, Frame 5 and BRUSH™ Power Generation generator technologies to meet accelerating power demand from data centers and energy infrastructure projects across North America. Awarded significant order to enable improved recovery, sustained production levels, and extension of field life in a mature offshore field in the Middle East. The scope includes nine electric motor-driven compressor trains for gas injection, gas lift, and boosting applications. Received a significant award from Saipem Nasser Saeed Al-Hajri Contracting Company (SNSH), a JV between Saipem and NSH in KSA, following a Novation Agreement with Aramco. The contract covers the supply of compression solutions for Aramco's Uthmaniyah conventional gas wells, supporting production optimization and enhanced recovery to extend the life of the field. The scope includes five electric motor-driven centrifugal compressor trains, together with associated balance-of-plant and auxiliary systems. Continued expanding IET’s presence into new markets, securing RINA certification for its fuel-flexible NovaLT™16 for maritime propulsion applications, specifically to operate on natural gas and up to 100% hydrogen to support maritime decarbonization. Grew digital solutions globally across a mix of software, hardware and services awards, leveraging the Company's Cordant™ Solutions portfolio to deploy asset performance software, analytics, and monitoring technologies through agreements with SINOPEC, Petrobras, and KNPC (formerly KIPIC) to enhance asset visibility and optimize operational performance. In addition, the Company secured a multi-year preferred supplier agreement with a global OEM to include vibration, sensing, condition monitoring, asset health software and services ─ supporting broader deployment across both new build and retrofit projects while driving greater standardization of asset protection and monitoring technologies. Oilfield Services & Equipment Oilfield Services & Equipment (“OFSE”) secured strategic orders and agreements across key product lines and geographies. Expanded the Company’s Norwegian presence and relationship with Equinor, strengthening North Sea capabilities. The Company inaugurated a new subsea manufacturing facility in Dusavik and announced two significant contract extensions for integrated drilling and well services solutions, as well as wireline intervention services. Secured a major contract extension and expansion with Petrobras for integrated well construction solutions across Brazil’s Santos Basin. The agreement builds on a 2024 well construction services award, further expanding the scope and impact of Baker Hughes’ integrated drilling solutions in the region. Signed significant contracts for wireline services with Oil and Natural Gas Corporation of India, to provide up to 46 advanced wireline units and integrated drill stem testing kits that will help improve reservoir insight, optimize production and support more efficient field development in offshore and onshore oil & gas fields. Secured a key milestone award for Leucipa™, marking its first deployment outside of the oil & gas sector. By integrating Baker Hughes’ ESP technology with the Leucipa™ digital optimization platform, the solution will support a geothermal and lithium extraction development in Europe through real-time monitoring, operational insights and performance optimization. Signed a strategic collaboration agreement with Helmerich & Payne, Inc. to support geothermal exploration and development in the United States. The companies will provide customers earlier access to dedicated rig capacity, reducing execution risk and allowing greater efficiency to move from project evaluation to development. Received a substantial subsea production systems contract from Azule Energy to support ultra-deepwater, greenfield development offshore Angola. Baker Hughes will manufacture and supply horizontal tree systems to enable safe, reliable and efficient production. Won a significant contract from McDermott to deliver integrated subsea systems for a natural gas development project offshore Brunei Darussalam. The scope includes six trees, controls, services, and subsea wellheads.
